Build APA text outputs from model results

Source: R/api-reports.R
build_apa_outputs.Rd

Build APA text outputs from model results

Print APA narrative text with preserved line breaks

Usage

build_apa_outputs(
  fit,
  diagnostics,
  bias_results = NULL,
  context = list(),
  whexact = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_apa_text'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_apa_outputs'
summary(object, top_n = 3, preview_chars = 160, ...)

Arguments

fit

Output from fit_mfrm().

diagnostics

Output from diagnose_mfrm().

bias_results

Optional output from estimate_bias().

context

Optional named list for report context.

whexact

Use exact ZSTD transformation.

x

Character text object from build_apa_outputs()$report_text.

...

Reserved for generic compatibility.

object

Output from build_apa_outputs().

top_n

Maximum non-empty lines shown in each component preview.

preview_chars

Maximum characters shown in each preview cell.

Value

An object of class mfrm_apa_outputs with:

  • report_text: APA-oriented Method/Results draft prose

  • decision: plain-language source-fit interpretation plus the separate uncertainty assessment; FormalInference is "Yes" only when both fit readiness and contract$precision$supports_formal_inference support it

  • fit_readiness, fit_readiness_components, and fit_readiness_parameters: exact source-fit readiness provenance

  • table_figure_notes: consolidated draft notes for tables/visuals

  • table_figure_captions: draft caption candidates without figure numbering

  • section_map: package-native section table for manuscript assembly

  • contract: draft content, uncertainty basis and source-fit checks

The input object (invisibly).

For summary(): An object of class summary.mfrm_apa_outputs.

Details

Use context to supply study information for the draft:

  • assessment, setting, scale_desc: assessment name, administration context and score scale.

  • rater_training, raters_per_response: training and assignment details.

  • rater_facet: facet label for reliability wording, subject to the agreement-summary restriction below.

  • line_width: text wrapping width for report_text (default 92).

For GPCM, this helper returns a caveated partial reporting bundle over supported diagnostics, direct tables, and plots. It also includes a gpcm_boundary table. Treat the output as slope-aware sensitivity-reporting text, not FACETS score-side equivalence, automatic operational scoring, or design-forecasting evidence.

By default, report_text includes:

  • model/data design summary (N, facet counts, scale range)

  • optimization/convergence metrics (Converged, Iterations, LogLik) plus the eligible canonical MML AIC/Person-BIC/SABIC panel or its explicit ineligibility and legacy-descriptive status; q<31 MML criteria are explicitly labelled screening/review-only rather than automatic ranking

  • anchor/constraint summary (noncenter_facet, centering convention, anchored levels, group anchors, dummy facets)

  • latent-regression population-model wording when fit has an active population_formula

  • category/threshold diagnostics (including disordered-step details when present)

  • overall fit, misfit count, and top misfit levels

  • facet reliability/separation, residual PCA summary, and bias-screen counts

  • stored inter-rater agreement, its matched-opportunity denominator and unavailable outcomes, separately from separation reliability

Agreement wording uses the rater facet in the stored diagnostics summary; context$rater_facet does not recalculate or relabel that summary. The model-expected baseline uses fitted category probabilities with calibration fixed, not marginal-frequency chance agreement. Adjacent agreement includes exact matches and differences of at most 1 on the compared score scale. Missing expected values remain explicit, including the stored number of opportunities without valid probabilities. An absent summary does not establish agreement. See interrater_agreement_table() for the matching, repeated-rating and denominator conventions.

Prints APA narrative text with preserved paragraph breaks using cat(). This is preferred over bare print() when you want readable multi-line report output in the console.

summary() method: Summarize APA report-output bundles

For summary(): Inspect component coverage, line/character counts and previews before reading the full draft.

Reviewing the draft

report_text is a third-person Method/Results draft; table_figure_notes and table_figure_captions provide matching notes and captions. Review them against the study record before manuscript use; these are not certifications of APA 7 or JARS compliance. Active latent-regression fits add a population section and Table 5 notes/captions distinguishing conditional-normal coefficients from post hoc regression on EAP/MLE scores.

Missing bias or PCA inputs cause those sections to be omitted. Reporting does not compute omitted PCA analyses: choose residual_pca = "overall", "facet" or "both" in diagnose_mfrm() first. For supported MML fits, diagnostic_mode = "both" retains plug-in and marginal diagnostics with different interpretations. Use summary(apa)$content_checks to check the draft against the supplied results, then read the full text.

Input validation

fit must be an mfrm_fit object from fit_mfrm(). diagnostics must be an mfrm_diagnostics object from diagnose_mfrm(). context must be a list (use NULL or list() for no extra context). If supplied, bias_results must come from estimate_bias() or another package-native bias helper that provides a table component.

Saved-result reuse

Supplied screening results must describe this fitted analysis. Results from another fit or older results without identity metadata are refused. See mfrmr_compatibility_layer to recreate them from the saved fit and matching diagnostics without refitting the model.

Interpreting output

The printed text is the same content stored in build_apa_outputs(...)$report_text, but with explicit paragraph breaks.

For summary():

  • overview: total coverage across standard text components.

  • decision: the source-fit decision shown before draft-completeness checks; text completeness cannot promote a review or blocked fit.

  • components: per-component density and mention checks (including residual-PCA mentions).

  • sections: package-native section coverage table.

  • content_checks: checks that draft text agrees with the supplied results.

  • overview$DraftContractPass: whether the expected information is present in draft text components.

  • overview$ReadyForAPA: a backward-compatible alias of that completeness flag, not a certification of inferential adequacy.

  • preview: first non-empty lines for fast visual review.

Typical workflow

  1. Generate apa <- build_apa_outputs(...).

  2. Print readable narrative with apa$report_text.

  3. Use summary(apa) to check completeness before manuscript use.

See also

build_visual_summaries(), estimate_bias(), mfrm_report_checklist, mfrmr_reporting_and_apa

build_apa_outputs(), base::summary()

Examples

# Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below.
# example("build_apa_outputs", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(mfrmr)

# Saved synthetic MML/RSM analysis of example_operational.
# For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm.
example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "operational-mml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example_fit$fit

# Use the diagnostics saved with this fit
diagnostics <- example_fit$diagnostics

# Prepare draft wording from the fitted model and diagnostics
apa <- build_apa_outputs(
  fit,
  diagnostics = diagnostics,
  context = list(
    assessment = "Synthetic writing assessment",
    setting = "Demonstration dataset",
    scale_desc = "1-4 rating scale",
    rater_facet = "Rater"
  )
)

# Check which sections are supported, then read the draft
apa_review <- summary(apa)
apa_review$content_checks
cat(apa$report_text)
# Adapt the text to the study question, design, and evidence before using it
} # }
# Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below.
# example("print.mfrm_apa_text", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Saved synthetic JML/RSM analysis of example_core.
# For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm.
example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "core-jml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example_fit$fit
diag <- example_fit$diagnostics
apa <- build_apa_outputs(fit, diag)
apa$report_text
} # }
# Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below.
# example("summary.mfrm_apa_outputs", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Saved synthetic JML/RSM analysis of example_core.
# For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm.
example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "core-jml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example_fit$fit
diag <- example_fit$diagnostics
apa <- build_apa_outputs(fit, diag)
summary(apa)
} # }
